subject: ConcordEdge preflight: encrypted storage zoning & heterogeneous node mix
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@concordedge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@concordedge.com
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ConcordEdge preflight: encrypted PV zoning + node mix questions

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick call this morning. We're lining up the on-prem cluster for the Proof of Concept and I wanted to confirm a few items so our facilities + security teams can finalize rack/network provisioning. Specific asks: 

1) Encryption: we need all persistent volumes encrypted at rest and a path to integrate our HSM-backed KMS. Do you require a particular KMS API compatibility (Vault, AzureKeyVault, AWS KMS)?

2) Storage zoning: we plan to land two classes of storage: 
   - fast local NVMe for model cache (read-dominant, ephemeral)
   - network-attached block (iSCSI/FC) for long-term checkpoints and logs
   Are there recommendations for how PV classes should be partitioned across node pools to meet eviction/latency SLOs?

3) Node mix: we anticipate mixing heterogeneous servers (2x A100 racks + 4x CPU-only for async tasks). Can Redwood runtime handle autoscaling across mixed instance types and do we need separate node pools for inference vs. data-processing?

4) Network egress: our compliance team requires an egress NAT and firewall rule list. Can you send a minimal set of IPs/ports Redwood needs?

If helpful, attaching our initial inventory (basic rack list) and a sketch of the site network.

Attachments: concordedge-preflight-inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-egress-diagram.pdf (diagram)

Appreciate the guidance — goal is to get a signed site acceptance checklist to our procurement team by next Wednesday.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Head of Site Ops — ConcordEdge
[Attachment: concordedge-preflight-inventory.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@concordedge.com>, ops@concordedge.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ConcordEdge preflight: encrypted PV zoning + node mix questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list, this is exactly what we need to move forward. Summary below with recommended defaults and a short checklist of info we still need from your side. I've attached a small inventory template to capture missing fields (hostname, NIC mapping, available local NVMe sizes).

High-level requirements / recommendations:

- Cluster footprint:
  * Control plane: 3 control-plane VMs (dedicated, non-schedulable) — we run control-plane services in the private deployment control plane; customer provides bare-metal VMs or co-located hosts.
  * Worker node pools (separate by function):
    - gpu-inference: tainted for inference workloads, GPUs (A100/RTX equivalent), local NVMe present for KV cache.
    - cpu-batch: for async preprocessing, smaller instance types, can be scaled horizontally.
    - infra-system: small, high-availability nodes for system daemons (monitoring, log-forwarders, CSI controllers).
    - storage-proxy (optional): if you are using a SAN/iSCSI backend that benefits from a caching/proxy tier, include 2-3 nodes with high-bandwidth links.

- PV class & zoning guidance:
  * pv-class:fast-nvme (local) — suitable for read-heavy KV cache and temporary model slices. Use ephemeral reclaim policy with a PV label to prevent eviction of active model shards.
  * pv-class:blockstore (network) — for checkpoints and logs; set retention via snapshot schedules.
  * Encryption: Redwood recommends encryption-at-rest be enforced at the storage layer (CSI-level encryption) backed by your KMS. If CSI does not support your KMS, we can fallback to host-level LUKS with customer-managed keys but must have key rotation and attestation requirements documented.

- KMS integration:
  * Supported: HashiCorp Vault (transit), AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault via CSI plugins. Provide endpoint, auth method (token/role), and network reachability.
  * We will need a service principal (or Vault role) that can issue DEK for CSI plugin. Please share the KMS access window for initial key provisioning.

- Networking / Egress:
  * Minimal outbound egress: 3 IPs (control-plane telemetry + update checks + metrics upload). We'll provide exact IP list after legal/ops signoff, but expect HTTPS (443) and NTP (123) to be required.
  * BGP/NAT: if you prefer no NAT, we support routing via customer BGP peering — note this requires a static route to Redwood management plane.

- Autoscaling & mixed instance types:
  * Redwood runtime supports mixed-type node pools. We strongly recommend distinct node pools per workload class to simplify scheduling and autoscaling (GPU-specific autoscalers vs CPU autoscalers).
  * Autoscaling triggers we recommend: queue depth for batched workloads, CPU utilization for background jobs, and GPU occupancy for inference lanes.

Checklist: items we still need from ConcordEdge to finalize preflight:
  1) Completed inventory template (attached) with NIC mappings and NVMe sizes.
  2) KMS endpoint + auth method (Vault role / AWS role / service principal).
  3) Preferred PV retention policy for checkpoint volume (days) and snapshot cadence.
  4) Network ACLs / firewall egress allowlist to permit initial provisioning.

I've attached "concordedge-preflight-inventory.xlsx" and a short text file with our KMS requirements for your security team (kms-requirements.txt).

Next step: once we have the inventory and KMS details, I'll schedule an on-site handoff call with our field engineering (karthik + infra) to walk the team through the node labeling, taints, and PV binding behavior.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@concordedge.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ConcordEdge preflight: encrypted PV zoning & node mix questions

Alex / team — quick technical notes from infra before the handoff call: 

- Taints & scheduling:
  * gpu-inference pool: add taint inference=dedicated:NoSchedule; use toleration only for runtime containers. 
  * cpu-batch: allow preemptible batch runners; scale-to-zero with KEDA from queue depth.

- CSI & encryption:
  * Recommend using a CSI driver that supports provider-side encryption (e.g., csi-vault + kms-plugin) so DEKs never touch disk in plaintext.
  * If you must use host-level LUKS, we need remote attestation (signed boot) and documented key-provisioning flow. Host-LUKS introduces upgrade/rollback risk.

- Storage performance & layout:
  * For model cache: use local NVMe configured as an XFS filesystem with mount options noatime,nodiratime and use an LVM thinpool if you need snapshotting. Keep the cache directories on a dedicated partition to avoid inode exhaustion.
  * For checkpoint volumes on iSCSI: ensure multipath is enabled on each node, and set io scheduler to none or mq-deadline depending on kernel version.
  * Snapshot cadence: daily snapshots for checkpoint volumes (retain 14 days) and hourly incremental for metadata that matters to your rollback policy.

- Node provisioning & monitoring:
  * Expose node-exporter + gpu-exporter on a private metrics port; provide us with a Prometheus scrape endpoint or allow outgoing to our metrics collection endpoint.
  * Host-level patches: we require a patching window and lifecycle plan (recommended: quarterly patching for non-critical nodes; monthly for infra nodes).

Open question for ConcordEdge security: do you require FIPS-mode kernels? If yes, we need to validate the CSI modules and nvme drivers for compatibility.

I'll be on the handoff call — happy to run through the taint/toleration examples and a short demo of PV binding behavior.

— Karthik
Principal Field Engineer — Redwood Inference
